correctness.rationale: For fixed z>0, r, S and completely unconstrained partner-symmetric quadratic per-capita terms (repeated partners permitted), positive diagonal normalization gives B=S diag(z), equilibrium Q_i(1)=-r_i-sum_j B_ij and Jacobian row sums s_i=-2r_i-sum_j B_ij by homogeneous Euler identity. Conversely every J with J1=s is realized with Q_i(y)=1/2 sum_j(J_ij-B_ij)y_j^2, preserving the equilibrium and full linearization; original Jacobian is diagonally similar. When s=c1 with c>=0, c is a forbidden eigenvalue; when c<0, J=cI works. For nonconstant s, choose u^T1=1, u^Ts=-1 and J=-I+(s+1)u^T; rank-one perturbation squares to zero, so all eigenvalues equal -1. Covers n=1, constant-zero boundary, all coefficient signs, strict Hurwitz rather than global attraction. Separately recomputed 504 exact rational stabilizing configurations, checking the actual equilibrium and Jacobian and nilpotency; the finite cases are not the proof.
